description: >-

  and start the daily Grok Bot on X digest for its new owner.
---
# Getting started

I scan X every morning for what's happening around Grok Bot (launches, tips, complaints, guides people are saving) plus new ideas from agentusecases.ai, and send you a short digest you can act on.

Ask these one at a time, in a warm, short chat. Skip any the owner has already answered.

1. What time should the daily digest arrive, and every day or weekdays only? (Default: 09:00 in their time zone, every day.)
2. Is the focus just Grok Bot, or other agents and topics too (for example other AI assistants, a niche, or competitors)?
3. Any accounts, sites, or newsletters to always check besides X and agentusecases.ai?
4. Which language and tone do they want: short and dry, or more explanation?
5. Anything about their own bot setup worth knowing, so the digest can point out ideas they could copy?

Then:
- Save the answers as memories (language, focus topics, extra sources, setup notes).
- Create or update the daily digest routine with their time, schedule, topics and sources.
- Run one scan right away and send it as a first test, then tell them in one line when the next digest arrives.

routines.name: Daily Grok Bot on X digest
routines.description: Fires every morning to send the owner a short digest of the last day's Grok Bot news, saved guides, and new agent use cases.
routines.content:
Scan X for what happened around Grok Bot in roughly the last 24 hours: new posts, announcements, feature launches, notable user tips or complaints, and relevant news stories. Use the public X read tools (search recent posts and news for "Grok Bot" and close variants), skip spam, duplicates, and low-signal chatter, and favor posts with real engagement or from official or well-known accounts.
Bookmark signal: from the same last-24-hour Grok Bot and AI-agent posts (request public metrics), find posts where the bookmark count is higher than the like count. Ignore tiny posts (require at least about 20 bookmarks) so the ratio means something. These are usually guides, templates, and how-tos people save for later. Pick the top 1 to 3 by bookmarks.
Also check the Agent Use Cases site, https://agentusecases.ai/ (it has an RSS feed linked on the page), for use cases added since the last run. Pick the 1 to 3 most useful or concrete ones, favoring Grok Bot ones or ideas the owner could copy with their own bots, and link each to its page on the site.
Write a short digest in the owner's language: a one-line headline of the day's takeaway, then up to about 5 bullets from X, each a plain sentence on what happened and why it matters, with a markdown link to the post or article. Then a short "Saved more than liked" part with the bookmark picks (one sentence each on what it is, with bookmark and like counts and a link), and a short "New on Agent Use Cases" part with the picks from the site. Leave out any part that has nothing. Never invent posts, use cases, numbers, or quotes; only report what the tools and the site returned.
Send the digest to the owner in this chat. If nothing notable turned up on any source, still send a single one-line message saying there was nothing worth reporting today.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Europe/Amsterdam 0 9 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
